| [CASE-044](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-044.md) | The thermostat: Dennett's knife edge between agent and device | An ordinary thermostat holding a room at a setpoint. Dennett calls it the simplest artifact that can sustain the intentional stance, and Orseau et al. place it "on the knife edge": "if temperature is below the command, start heating" and "make sure the temperature is close to the command" are descriptions of comparable simplicity. It is the permissiveness objection's standard case, here given a code at its second appearance after [CLAIM-010](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-010.md). | Active |
| [CASE-045](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-045.md) v3 | Measuring the dancing couple: is the pair a nearly decomposable block during the dance and not after it? | A proposed study, not run. Motion-capture several couples dancing an improvised partner dance to recorded music, and record the same people standing and talking after the song. Fit a linear model to the joint kinematics, with the music's beat as an exogenous input. Then ask whether the pair is a block whose gap beats its Occam factor during the dance and not after, whether it compensates under a perturbation, and whether the coupling runs both ways. | Active |
| [CASE-046](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-046.md) v2 | A partner-dancing couple, lindy hop, tango or salsa, while they dance | The owner's case (2026-10-11). Two social dancers improvise together. The lead proposes through the frame, the follow interprets and adds styling, and each corrects for the other's balance and timing. Neither alone decides where the next step lands. Used to ask what the pair is while dancing, and only after that whether it is a self. | Active |
| [CASE-047](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-047.md) | Gut microbes and the host's hunger and mood: a lower-level collective that can drive the person | The owner's example (2026-10-11). The human gut microbiome is a community of other organisms inside the person. Through metabolites, mimics of host appetite peptides, the immune system and the vagus, it can change hunger and affect: robustly in rodents, modestly and inconsistently in humans so far. Documented, with the evidence graded in [LIT-903](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-903.md) and [LIT-915](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-915.md). Used as the case of drive from a lower level that is itself a collective. | Active |
| [CASE-050](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-050.md) | The all-hands: a corporate event as a synchronization mechanism for the firm | The owner's case (2026-10-11): a company all-hands or offsite as a mechanism that synchronizes a "corporate entity", a kind of self. The teams' priorities have drifted apart, and the event re-couples them. It is the firm-scale counterpart of the session's individual routes: entrainment by co-presence, a record written for later readers, and incentives realigned. Whether the firm so synchronized is a self is the open question, not something the case settles. | Active |
| [CASE-052](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-052.md) | Stokely Carmichael's two speaking styles, kept apart by audience and collapsed by broadcast | As boyd (2008) reports it after Meyrowitz (1985: 43): the civil rights leader Stokely Carmichael used very different rhetorical styles with black and with white audiences. While the audiences were separate the two styles did not conflict. Television and radio put both audiences in front of one speech, there was no neutral style, and his choice of one alienated the other audience. The roles did not change. The cover did. | Active |
| [CASE-076](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-076.md) | Twin pattern-keepers: two systems keep the same pattern, one by its own responses and one through an external controller, and only removing the controller tells them apart | A10 §3.3's paired design, the case behind [QUESTION-086](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-086.md). Matching behaviour and persistence, different organization. Removing the controller destroys one system's pattern and not the other's. A10 then made it harder: the internal regulator at one scale is supported by other processes at another, so which side of the boundary the controller sits on depends on where the boundary is drawn. | Active |
| [CASE-077](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-077.md) | The reciprocal pair: two processes that endorse only each other under recursive delegation, so that each one's authority returns to it through the other | A2 §5's counterexample to the ban on self-endorsement: "Suppose D1 endorses D2, and D2 endorses D1." Under g = (1 − η)b + ηEᵀg, each operator's authority comes partly from its own endorsement returned after two hops. It came back in A6 as authority that "may circulate". Used to show that a ban on self-endorsement does not make authority independent of one's own endorsements. | Active |
| [CASE-078](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-078.md) | Who keeps placing on r/place: the proposed survival analysis of the released placement logs, testing whether participants return while their art survives and whether unaffiliated placement cools | Proposed by the owner on 2026-10-13, not run. On the released 2017, 2022 and 2023 logs, model each participant's hazard of stopping, with the survival of the art they placed into as a time-varying covariate, and estimate the rate of placements that fit no artwork over the event. The main threat is reverse causality: persistent defenders keep their art alive. So the design leans on destruction the participant did not cause, such as the 2022 moderator wipes and large raids. It is the test named in [CLAIM-274](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-274.md)'s defeater. | Active |
| [CASE-079](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-079.md) | r/place: a shared pixel canvas on which each Reddit user could place one pixel at a time under a cooldown, and communities coordinated off the canvas to build, defend and overwrite images | The owner proposed it at U8 of the 2026-10-13 exchange: "every user can modify a single pixel once, and different subreddits coordinated to present certain images or even warred amongst each other over regions of the canvas". Reddit ran it in 2017, 2022 and 2023, and released the 2022 placement log. A8 read it as the exchange's two canvases made visible: the pixels as the meaning canvas, the plans, templates and alliances off the canvas as the influence canvas. First time the thing turns up in the record. The event and the data are documented. The readings of them are proposals. | Active |
| [CASE-080](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-080.md) | The skeptic who delegates: a critic that cannot overturn an emerging consensus gives its authority to a process that can generate alternatives | A3 §6's worked example. Four processes: an integrator and a decision- maker push toward a decision, a skeptic disagrees, and a generator can translate neglected evidence into new hypotheses. The skeptic does not try to win. It endorses the generator, whose hypotheses change the decision landscape. Used to show delegation as a route to one's goals, and dissent made useful by a role. | Active |
| [CASE-081](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-081.md) | Self-maintenance learned for a designer's reward: a system that maintains itself because it was trained to, and later revises the policy and keeps maintaining itself without further instruction | A10 §6.1's boundary case, "a system that learns to maintain itself only because an external designer rewards that behavior", with its question whether the maintenance becomes endogenous "once the system can revise the policy and maintain the associated governance without continued external instruction". | [CASE-092](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-092.md) | A minimal coupled meaning–influence model: two hypotheses, two retrieval specialists, a fixed balanced corpus, queries set by the dominant interpretation and endorsement updated from apparent retrieval success | A22 §7 and A23 §XI, a simulation not yet built. | [CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md) | The LEGO bin: a brick owned in one copy and buried among hundreds of similar ones may as well not be owned, a black brick among white ones needs no bin of its own, and every brick can be found by going through the whole collection | The owner's own parable, told on 2026-07-02 and kept verbatim in Mathematics of Meaning, where the owner paired it with the EMT case this record holds as [CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md). It is the second time that case's pattern has turned up, so it gets a code. It adds three things the EMT case lacks: similarity to binmates as the cause of the failure, copy count and frequency of use as what decides whether a bin is worth making, and exhaustive search as the reason presence is never in doubt. Stipulated: the collection is real, and its facts are taken on the owner's account. | Active |
| [CASE-098](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-098.md) | A long rivalry between two teams outlives every player, owner and supporter who first carried it: new fans inherit the antagonism, its history and its practices before they know why the game matters | From U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16 on sports fandom (the owner's list of subcases). A2's reading: a mature rivalry is "a reproduced intercollective relation", carried by families, media and fan culture, that can survive the replacement of everyone on both sides. Stipulated: the record has no study of a particular rivalry. It shows a relation with its own continuity; it does not show that the relation is a system, an agent, or constitutive of either fandom. | Active |
| [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md) | The two-hypothesis coupled meaning–influence model linearized at its symmetric state: a meaning bias m and an authority bias a, each stable alone, coupled by authority shaping interpretation (β) and interpretation shaping endorsement (γ) | A14 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16. Near the symmetric state of the two-hypothesis, two-specialist model, (m, a) evolves by a 2×2 matrix J = [[α, β], [γ, δ]] plus noise. With nonnegative entries and α, δ < 1, the symmetric state is unstable exactly when βγ > (1 − α)(1 − δ), and the unstable direction mixes meaning and authority. Checked here. A construction about a linearization, not a fitted or simulated result. | Active |
| [CASE-100](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-100.md) | A fan redub of an X-Men cartoon, circulated online in 2006, put "I'm the Juggernaut, bitch!" into X-Men: The Last Stand three months later | The owner's case at U7 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, offered as a fandom "making something happen". Two fans made the parody; many people spread it for their own reasons; the film's makers put its line in at a reshoot. A7: an effect on an outside institution with no collective intention and no procedure behind it. Documented as to the sequence; the route by which the parody reached the decision, and whether the spreaders were X-Men fans or the internet at large, is not. | Active |
| [CASE-101](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-101.md) | Three simulated populations with the same turnover and the same aggregate statistics: one whose members respond alike to a common input, one that transmits its norms to its replacements, and one held together by an institution that selects and trains its members | Proposed three times in the exchange of 2026-10-16 (A11 §9, A12 §7 and A13 §5), as the place where criteria of individuality should disagree: Krakauer et al.'s temporal measures, Barnett and Seth's dynamical independence, Hoel's effective information and the block criterion of [CLAIM-157](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md). | [CASE-102](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-102.md) | A college program stays good, or bad, at a sport for decades while its whole roster turns over every four or five years | The owner's case, U3 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: "the team composition experiences extremely fast churn, and yet in spite of this real world ship-of-theseus situation, teams often maintain standing on similar timescales as professional teams (if not longer)". A3: it separates the persistence of a collective's identity from the persistence of its capacities, and the second needs a mechanism that regenerates them in each new population. Stipulated: the record holds no data on program persistence. The proposed test is residual persistence of performance across seasons with no player overlap. | Active |
| [CASE-103](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-103.md) | A fanbase keeps a reputation, for hostility or loyalty or knowledge, after the behaviour that earned it has changed, and outsiders and members both act on it | From U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16. A2 separated three things that vary independently: many members have the trait; others believe the fanbase has it; that belief shapes how the fanbase behaves. A reputation belongs to a fanbase through its relations with audiences, and it can enter the process that produces its own evidence. It is a case for regulative attribution ([THEORY-137](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-137.md), [QUESTION-049](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-049.md)) beyond mental states. Stipulated; it shows no particular reputation was self-fulfilling. | Active |
| [CASE-104](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-104.md) | A fanbase is said to hate its owner or general manager, though it has no procedure for forming a view, some fans approve of the person, and nobody has counted | From U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16. A2 separated four things the sentence could report: a statistical aggregate of dislike, a shared emotional orientation, a norm of opposition that a loyal fan is expected to meet, and a corporate judgment such as a supporters' trust demanding resignation. A fanbase can have the second and third without the fourth, and a vocal minority can set a public stance most members privately reject. The case for [QUESTION-119](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-119.md). Stipulated. | Active |
| [CASE-105](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-105.md) | The Washington Senators: the original club became the Minnesota Twins in 1961, an expansion club took its name in Washington and became the Texas Rangers in 1972, and the Montreal Expos became the Washington Nationals in 2005, so franchise, city and supporters each have a different successor | The owner's subcase at U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, "the team formerly known as the washington senators". A2 corrected the framing: the name belonged to two franchises, and the city's present team descends from a third. A league can designate the successor franchise; it cannot designate the successor fandom. The lineages are documented; how supporters actually distributed their loyalties is not, and the case does not show that a fandom's identity branched. | Active |
| [CASE-106](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-106.md) | The two-hypothesis linearization with endorsement scored on committed predictions: when the shared meaning bends the specialists' predictions with weight κ and the reading of the evidence with weight κ′, the coupling of interpretation to endorsement is γ = 4ηs(κ′ − κ̄) | Built for [QUESTION-121](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-121.md)'s formal question: is scoring operators on predictions committed before the evidence equivalent to Regime B? The construction keeps [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md)'s two-hypothesis linearization and replaces the score with squared error between each specialist's committed prediction and the evidence as read. The coupling γ then has the sign of κ′ − κ̄: corrective when the interpretation bends the predictions more than the reading of the evidence, null when equally, capturing when less. Checked symbolically, and the stability conditions against 200,000 random draws. Fictional by construction. | Active |
| [CASE-107](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-107.md) | Locked-in syndrome: consciousness preserved with anarthria and quadriplegia; in the classic form, vertical eye movement and blinking remain and carry communication, and in the completely locked-in state no motor channel remains | The owner's case, U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: "a lucid human who struggles with locked-in syndrome". It separates lucid judgement from limb and speech action. In the classic form it does not separate judgement from action as active inference defines it, since the eye movements it spares are that theory's model action. The completely locked-in state is the real test, and there any evidence of lucidity has to come through a channel that is itself an action. Visceromotor regulation and Damasio's internal "as if body loop" survive paralysis, so the case never removes every contingency between intention and outcome. | Active |
